$comment: Time-boxed exceptions to the blocking high/critical npm-audit gate.
An entry here is a DEBT RECORD, not a dismissal. Every field is load-bearing,
and since H60 (2026-08-18) check-audit.mjs ENFORCES that — a missing field is
a MALFORMED failure, because an entry with no `revisitAfter` compares
`undefined < today` === false and so never expires: it switches its own
time-box off, which is the one property that stops this file decaying into a
suppression list.
advisory      the GHSA id, so the entry is greppable against the report
package       the vulnerable package (NOT the transitive parents)
workspace     which lockfile it lives in
severity      as reported by npm audit
why           why it is not fixable TODAY — must name what was tried
reachability  the honest exploitability call, with the evidence for it
revisitAfter  ISO date. PAST THIS DATE THE BUILD FAILS. Not a snooze —
it forces the assessment to be re-made, not inherited.
removeWhen    the concrete condition that retires this entry
owner         which surface owns the decision — an exception nobody owns
is nobody's to revisit
mitigation    the compensating control that exists TODAY. An exception with
no stated mitigation is a dismissal in a justification's
clothes.
check-audit.mjs also fails on a STALE entry (listed but no longer reported),
so a fixed advisory cannot quietly keep its exception — and it matches on the
ADVISORY, never the package name, so an entry cannot silently absorb a NEW
advisory that lands on the same package.

why: ADDED 2026-08-18 (H61). This entry exists for a copy `npm audit` CANNOT
SEE. unpdf declares no `pdfjs-dist` dependency; it BUNDLES pdf.js into
node_modules/unpdf/dist/pdfjs.mjs. Measured today: unpdf@1.6.2 bundles
apiVersion 5.6.205, inside GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j's range (>=5.6.83 <6.2.108).
So the KB's PRIMARY PDF path carried the advisory while the audit, this
file and every CI gate reported clean. The advisory was already recorded
twice (officeparser, pdfjs-dist) for the SECOND PDF path — nothing tied
those records to the invisible one.
NO UPSTREAM FIX EXISTS. unpdf@1.8.1 (latest) bundles ~6.1.200, still below
6.2.108. There is no version to bump to, so this is not a deferred bump.
VENDORED (2026-09-27): npm audit cannot see this copy, so check-audit's
STALE arm does not judge it — #4166 fixed the audit-visible pdfjs-dist
copies and the advisory id vanished from the report, while this bundled
pdf.js (5.6.205) is still inside the range. Its staleness is enforced by
test/kb-vendored-pdfjs.test.ts, which reds once the bundle is fixed.
RE-ASSESSED 2026-09-29 (revisitAfter 2026-09-30 → 2026-10-14). Re-measured, not
inherited: npm's latest unpdf is still 1.8.1 (published 2026-08-13; no release
since), and its dist/pdfjs.mjs apiVersion is 6.1.200, still inside the range
(<6.2.108). The installed copy is unpdf 1.6.2 (pdf.js 5.6.205). Bumping to 1.8.1
would not leave the range, so there is still nothing to take. The mitigation
is still in place: `isEvalSupported: false` at kbService.ts's getDocumentProxy
call. Containment (the bounded extraction worker) is still NOT in place, so the
reachability call below stands unchanged.
reachability: AUTHENTICATED UPLOAD ONLY, and it is the DEFAULT PDF path — every
application/pdf upload reaches it (features/kb/kbService.ts), unlike the
officeparser copy which needs an office MIME or a magic-byte reroute.
GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j is 'arbitrary JavaScript execution upon opening a
malicious PDF' (CWE-79), written against the browser viewer. Server-side
text extraction is a narrower surface — it renders nothing — but narrower
is not assessed, and the input is untrusted bytes either way.
exceptions.removeWhen: unpdf publishes a release bundling pdf.js >= 6.2.108 — then bump unpdf, DELETE this entry, and `test/kb-vendored-pdfjs.test.ts` will fail until you do (it asserts the entry is gone once the bundled version is fixed). MEASURED 2026-08-18: unpdf@1.8.1 bundles ~6.1.200, so there is nothing to take yet.
mitigation: `isEvalSupported: false` is now passed at the app-controlled
getDocumentProxy call (H61). pdf.js defaults it to TRUE — i.e. the parser
was permitted to evaluate strings as JavaScript while parsing untrusted
uploads. That removes the eval path this advisory is about on THIS call
site; it is not a patch, and it does not cover officeparser's own copy,
which the app does not configure.
Visibility, which is the point of this entry, is enforced by
test/kb-vendored-pdfjs.test.ts: it reads the bundled apiVersion and fails
if the vendored copy is vulnerable and unrecorded, or recorded and no
Containment (a bounded extraction worker on the ADR 0555 child adapter) is
NOT in place; extraction still runs in the API process with only a 32 MiB

why: ADDED 2026-09-30. Published 2026-09-30 against @grpc/grpc-js (patched in 1.14.5).
The frontend copy is @grpc/grpc-js@1.9.16, pulled ONLY by firebase@12.13.0 ->
@firebase/firestore@4.14.1 (+ firestore-compat). Tried: npm's suggested fix is a
semver-MAJOR firebase downgrade (to 9.14.0) - not acceptable. Measured upstream:
the LATEST @firebase/firestore (4.17.2, in firebase 12.19.0) still pins
@grpc/grpc-js '~1.9.0', so no firebase version leaves the range. Forcing an npm
override to 1.14.x under firestore's ~1.9 pin is an unsupported combination for a
code path we do not use (below). The backend copy WAS bumped to 1.14.5 in the same
PR (which also cleared GHSA-f596-whhp-79r4 there; f596 does not match 1.9.16).
reachability: NOT REACHABLE. (1) The SPA never imports Firestore: `grep -rn firestore
frontend/react/src` finds nothing; the only firebase imports are firebase/app +
firebase/auth (src/auth/firebase.ts, lazily). (2) @grpc/grpc-js is Firestore's NODE
transport; the browser build of @firebase/firestore uses WebChannel and never
bundles grpc-js, so it cannot ship in dist/ even if Firestore were imported.
exceptions.removeWhen: @firebase/firestore depends on @grpc/grpc-js >=1.14.5 (bump firebase), or firebase is removed from the frontend.
exceptions.mitigation: Firestore is not imported by the SPA and grpc-js is Node-only, so no shipped bundle contains it; the backend copy is patched (1.14.5).

why: ADDED 2026-09-30. @grpc/grpc-js reaches frontend/react ONLY through the `firebase`
meta-package's @firebase/firestore(+compat), which pin `@grpc/grpc-js ~1.9.0`.
Every 1.9.x (latest 1.9.16) is inside the advisory range (<=1.13.5), including
@firebase/firestore@latest (4.17.2 via firebase@12.19.0). npm's only offered fix
is a MAJOR DOWNGRADE to firebase@9.14.0, which is not a fix. An `overrides` pin
to 1.14.x would put grpc-js outside Firestore's declared range for code this
app does not ship. The backend copy WAS fixed (1.14.4 → 1.14.5, in range).
Advisory: server transmits method-handler error messages to the client (server-side).
RECONCILED 2026-09-30: #4282 excepted only GHSA-m9gg for this package; this
second advisory passed ONLY because check-audit's matcher let one exception
waive a package's other advisories (fixed in the same change as this entry).
reachability: UNREACHABLE in what this workspace ships, MEASURED 2026-09-30 on the production
build: the SPA imports only `firebase/app` and `firebase/auth` (static + dynamic
imports; no firestore/database/storage/functions/messaging anywhere in src/).
`dist/` contains ZERO references to grpc-js and no `http2` transport; the only
`@firebase/firestore` string is firebase/app's platform-logger name table, not
code. grpc-js is a Node-only library and both advisories are SERVER-side
(a grpc server's getAuthContext; a server leaking handler error messages).
The browser has no grpc server and loads no grpc-js.
exceptions.removeWhen: @firebase/firestore depends on a grpc-js outside the advisory range, OR the SPA replaces the `firebase` meta-package with `@firebase/app` + `@firebase/auth` (which removes grpc-js from this lockfile entirely) — then DELETE this entry.
exceptions.owner: Frontend auth — frontend/react/src/auth/firebase.ts (the only firebase consumer)
exceptions.mitigation: Nothing that loads grpc-js is shipped to browsers; any new `firebase/firestore` import would change that and must re-open this entry. The frontend build's bundle budget + this re-assessment date are the tripwires.
